To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) transpiration and yield of bell pepper are increased when irrigation water salinity increases, but only up to a certain level; (ii) leaching is needed for maintaining low soil solution salinity and high yield; and (iii) the leaching requirements for high yields increase with irrigation water salinity.

(1) leaching fraction was found not to be linearly dependent on the amount of applied water and (2) the higher the salinity of the irrigation water, the higher the leaching fraction that should be applied to maximize yield.

the amount of water needed to maximize yield when irrigating with a given saline water depends strongly on the salinity level of the irrigation water, and that leaching fraction is a strong function of plant water uptake.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between the salinity of the irrigation water and the amount of water applied.
the effects of irrigation water salinities on the leaching requirements and transpiration needs of bell peppers.
the effect of irrigation water salinization on the transpiration and leaching requirements of bell peppers in protected growing environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of irrigation water salinization on transpiration and yields depends on plant species, on soil properties, and on the extent of leaching.
the higher the salinity of the irrigation water, the greater the leaching requirement for maximizing crop yields.
the effect of irrigation water salinization on crop yields depends on the extent of leaching and on the extent to which plant growth is limited by the salinity of the root zone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of saline water should be limited to crops with low sensitivity to salinity.
, when irrigating with water of salinity higher than 3 dS/m, it would be better to apply less water and to increase the salinity level in order to minimize leaching requirements.
, in general, the higher the salinity of the irrigation water, the greater the amount of irrigation needed to maximize crop yields.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amount of water needed to maintain a given salinity in the soil solution depends on the plant's response to salinity, and this response is not known for many crops.
the effect of irrigation water salinities on crop yield is highly dependent on water quantity.
when irrigating with high salinity water, the leaching fraction should be kept low to minimize the amount of applied water and to maximize the amount of water available for crop transpiration.
